name: cmsis-developer-assistant
description: Enable AI coding agents to develop and debug CMSIS projects with AI skills and MCP tools.

commands.title: Import a File for This Document…

cmsis-developer-assistant.timeoutInSecon.description: Timeout in seconds for debugging operations

cmsis-developer-assistant.serverPort.description: Port number for the CMSIS Developer Assistant server

enumDescriptions: The setup offers to add the tool rules to your agents' rule files, and offers to update blocks written earlier when a release changes the rules.
The setup never offers it, and no rule file is touched.
cmsis-developer-assistant.agentRules.ins.markdownDescription: Whether **CMSIS Developer Assistant: Configure Agent** — also the first-run setup — offers to add the tool rules, which keep agents on the MCP tools instead of `pyocd`, `gdb` or `cbuild` in a shell, to your agents' rule files: `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`, `~/.codex/AGENTS.md` and `~/.copilot/copilot-instructions.md` (preselected), or a workspace's `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md` and the rule folders of Cursor, Cline and Roo Code. Every change is shown as a diff and written only when you confirm it; the rules sit between `cmsis-developer-assistant:rules` marker comments and nothing else in the file changes. When a release changes the rules, activation offers once to review the update of the blocks written earlier; each file is shown as a diff and written only when you confirm it, and no block is ever created at activation. `never`: the setup skips the step and no rule file is touched.

cmsis-developer-assistant.redactSecrets.markdownDescription: Withhold variable and expression values whose name or content looks like a credential (API key, token, password, connection string) before they are sent to an AI agent. Numeric scalars are never withheld, so firmware flags and counters named `auth`, `token` or `key` stay readable. Raw target reads — `read_memory`, `read_core_registers`, `read_peripheral_register`, `get_fault_info`, and GDB commands passed through `evaluate_expression` as `-exec …` or `>…` — are never redacted.

cmsis-developer-assistant.dapRequestTime.description: Per-request timeout (in milliseconds) for DAP traffic to the debug adapter / hardware probe. If the probe or GDB server stalls, requests will fail with a HardwareTimeoutError instead of hanging the MCP tool call. Increase for slow targets or large memory reads.

cmsis-developer-assistant.memoryReadTime.description: Overall timeout (in milliseconds) for a single read_memory / read_core_registers tool call. Caps the total time spent talking to the hardware, even across many word-level fallback reads.

cmsis-developer-assistant.build.diagnost.markdownDescription: After a failed CMSIS build, run `cbuild` once more with `--log` — without downloading packs, updating RTE files or cleaning — so that the `cmsis_action build` result can show the compiler, linker and ninja error lines with file and line. The CMSIS Solution extension keeps no build log of its own. The same re-run checks a build that exited 0 but did not rewrite its image, since CMSIS Solution reports exit 0 for failed builds too. The re-run is incremental, stops after 30 min, when another build starts or on `cmsis_action stop_build`, and writes `out/cmsis-developer-assistant/build-diagnostic.log` next to the solution; a re-run stopped at the limit or by `stop_build` reports only what it printed before the stop. Off: the result still shows the errors csolution records in the solution's `cbuild-idx.yml`, and such a build is reported as not confirmed. Not used with a CMSIS Solution that hands out the exit code and output it captured for a build (API version 3): the result is then the build's own. Applies to the next build.

cmsis-developer-assistant.telemetry.json.markdownDescription: Append one JSON line per MCP tool call — tool name, argument and result size in bytes, duration, outcome — to this file, for offline analysis of what an agent session costs. Empty (the default) keeps the file off; the in-memory statistics behind `get_session_status` and the `cmsis-developer-assistant://stats` resource are always kept. A relative path is resolved against the first workspace folder. Read once at activation: changing it needs a window reload. The file records names and sizes only, never tool arguments or results.

cmsis-developer-assistant.serial.enabled.markdownDescription: Offer the `serial_*` tools (UART ports and the Serial Monitor) to AI agents. Off removes the eleven serial tools from the MCP tool list, which every agent turn carries — worth it when your workflow never reads a UART. Read once at activation: changing it needs a window reload, and it applies to the next agent connection.

cmsis-developer-assistant.serial.idleClo.markdownDescription: Release a serial port an AI agent opened with `serial_open` after this many seconds without a serial tool call (`serial_read`, `serial_write`, `serial_status`, `serial_clear_buffer`), so the Serial Monitor or a terminal can open it again. Bytes the board sends do not count as use. `0` turns the idle release off; a port is still released when the agent's MCP session ends. Read at each `serial_open`: no reload needed.

cmsis-developer-assistant.packDocs.enabl.markdownDescription: Offer the documentation tools to AI agents: `list_target_docs`, `search_target_docs`, `read_doc_pages`, `fetch_doc`, `get_peripheral_docs` — page-cited search over the reference manuals, datasheets, errata and board manuals the current csolution target's DFP/BSP ship or link, plus Arm documents, your own imported manuals and the workspace `docs/` folder. On by default; off drops the five tools from the MCP tool list every agent turn carries. PDFs are indexed with the bundled pdf.js (poppler optional, see `packDocs.extractor`). Read once at activation: changing it needs a window reload.

cmsis-developer-assistant.packDocs.extra.markdownDescription: PDF text extractor. `pdfjs` is bundled and needs nothing installed (what `auto` uses); `pdftotext` uses poppler from the PATH or `packDocs.pdftotextPath`. Switching re-extracts documents on their next use.

cmsis-developer-assistant.packDocs.pdfto.description: Executable name or path of pdftotext, used when packDocs.extractor is pdftotext.

cmsis-developer-assistant.packDocs.maxPd.description: PDFs larger than this (in MB) are listed but not indexed.

cmsis-developer-assistant.packDocs.inven.description: When fetch_doc cannot get a document the CMSIS view lists, write the reason into that document's error in CMSIS Solution's ~/.cmsis/docs.yml, so the view shows what the agent waits for. Only that one field of that one entry is changed, and cleared again when a later fetch succeeds.

enumDescriptions: CMSIS Solution's document service when it offers one, else the one built into this extension (a prototype of what CMSIS Solution should provide), which shares CMSIS Solution's folder ~/.cmsis/.
Always the document service built into this extension.
cmsis-developer-assistant.packDocs.docum.description: Who keeps the target's documents, their downloads, the documents you add (for you or the project, in .cmsis/docs.yml) and the agent's requests. The built-in service keeps them where CMSIS Solution does: the inventory ~/.cmsis/docs.yml and the copies under ~/.cmsis/docs/. The search index is always this extension's: beside each of those copies, and in its own storage for the PDFs of packs and workspaces.

cmsis-developer-assistant.packDocs.inclu.description: Also list PDFs found inside the device/board pack that no <book> element references.

cmsis-developer-assistant.packDocs.works.markdownDescription: Folders (relative to each workspace folder) whose PDFs are listed and searched together with the target's pack documents — the drop folder for a datasheet or manual the packs do not ship.

cmsis-developer-assistant.packDocs.userD.markdownDescription: The retired user documents folder (empty: `~/.cmsis-pack-docs/user`). The documentation tools no longer read it, and nothing moves or changes it: when it still holds PDFs, the extension says so once. Add the documents you still need to a target with **Add Document** or **Import Document for Current Target**, then delete the folder.

cmsis-developer-assistant.buildInfo.enab.markdownDescription: Offer the build-artefact tools to AI agents: `list_build_artifacts`, `get_memory_usage`, `lookup_symbol`, `get_section_layout`, `get_build_diagnostics` — the ELF, linker map and build log of the current csolution target, read deterministically. On by default; off drops the five tools from the MCP tool list every agent turn carries. Read once at activation: changing it needs a window reload.

cmsis-developer-assistant.buildInfo.maxS.description: Symbols and objects listed by get_memory_usage and get_section_layout (the tool's top argument overrides it).

cmsis-developer-assistant.buildInfo.logG.markdownDescription: Workspace globs searched for build logs by `get_build_diagnostics` (newest first). After a failed build, `cmsis_action build` writes one into `out/cmsis-developer-assistant/build-diagnostic.log`.

cmsis-developer-assistant.sourceBrowsing.markdownDescription: **Experimental**, and therefore off by default: the tools, their arguments and their output may change between releases. Offer the source-browsing tools to AI agents: `source_find` says what a C or C++ symbol is, where it is declared and defined, and what can be asked about it; `source_get` returns its definition, references, callers, callees, supertypes, subtypes or implementations. Both answer from the clangd the editor runs, through the clangd extension of the Keil Studio Pack, for the context CMSIS Solution set up (`cmsis-csolution.generateClangSetup`); nothing is downloaded or configured by these tools, and a missing clangd is reported in the tool's answer. Read once at activation: changing it needs a window reload.

cmsis-developer-assistant.knowledge.inde.markdownDescription: Path of a knowledge index (`knowledge.db`) that replaces the core index the extension ships (`resources/knowledge/core.db`), for testing a rebuilt index. Empty uses the core index. Absolute, starting with `~`, or relative to the first workspace folder. Read on every call. The knowledge tools are always on.

cmsis-developer-assistant.knowledge.incl.markdownDescription: Also return knowledge units whose text is still a placeholder, such as an error message without a recorded cause. Off leaves them out of `knowledge_search`; a build result never names them.

scripts.pretest: npm run compile && npm run lint
scripts.test:transport: npm run compile && node test/transport/session-lifecycle.js && node test/transport/two-window-routing.js
scripts.tpip:report: tsx scripts/tpip-reporter --header docs/tpip-header.md --knowledge resources/knowledge/SOURCES.md docs/third-party-licenses.json TPIP.md
